full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Sontosh Kumar Shaha, was appointed as probationer Assistant Judge in the subordinate judiciary through the competitive BCS examination, held in the year 1985, and was posted at Bogra on 30.1.1998. The subordinate Judiciary is controlled by the Ministry of Law, Government of Bangladesh, After his confirmation in the service and wonderful performance in discharging duties, he was posted as Senior Assistant Judge on 14.03.2000 after proper recommendation by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Thereafter during the tenure of the service when he became eligible for promotion to the next post, his name was posted at Serial No.37 in the promotion list of the Subordinate Judge Panel along with others. Thereafter when the petitioner was posted at Chuadanga and serving as Senior Assistant Judge the Respondent No.1 issued an order under Rule 3(d) of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1985 raising allegation against the petitioner of corruption and other offences and purportedly obtained approval from the Supreme Court as to initiation of departmental proceeding against the petitioner without actually having any approval from neither the G. A. Committee nor from the full court of the High Court Division and only got a nod from the honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh. Thereafter two departmental case, one being No.4 of 2000 dated 16.10.2000 and other being No.3 of 2000 dated 18.10.2000 was initiated against the petitioner and accordingly two charge sheets were served upon the petitioner, asking him to show cause, within 10 days, as to why he shall not be proceeded with for the alleged offence committed. The petitioner duly submitted the reply on 01.11.2000 denying all the material allegations. Thereafter the learned District Judge Mr. Azizul Hoque was appointed as Inquiry Officer to hold enquiry into the allegation raised against the petitioner. The petitioner by filing application raised objection against the Inquiry officer and prayed for his change on the ground that he had some enmity with the Inquiry officer but without any success. The said Inquiry Officer without following the procedure and without giving the proper opportunity of being heard to the petitioner held the enquiry and upon getting no evidence as to the allegation, as raised against the petitioner submitted his report on 20.5.2000 stating the same accordingly. The respondent No.1, upon getting the report from the Inquiry officer and having found that the petitioner is not guilty of the offence. passed an order recommending the exoneration of the petitioner from the allegation, which was also approved by Hon'ble Minister of Law on 07.1.2002. The Ministry of Law sent the said recommendation to the Registrar of the Bangladesh Supreme Court. Respondent No.2 on 17.1.2002 praying for approval from the Supreme Court in respect of withdrawal of suspension and the departmental proceedings against the petitioner in departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000. Similarly the Respondent No.1 having found that the petitioner is not guilty of the offence as alleged in departmental proceeding No.4 of 2000 sent a further letter to the Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court. Respondent No.2 praying for exonerating the petitioner from, the allegation as brought against him in the said departmental proceeding. But the said recommendation being not approved by the Supreme Court. the Ministry of Law sought further consideration of the said refusal of approval of the recommendation on two other occasions without any success and thereafter served the second show cause notice upon the petitioner on 20.11.2003. Challenging the same the petitioner preferred Writ Petition No.7316 of 2003 and their Lordships in the High Court Division on motion hearing, called for record from the Respondent No.2, Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court to have a clarification on the point whether the proposed order of suspension and the proposal for withdrawal of suspension of the petitioner made in departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000 and 4 of 2000 were submitted before the General Administration Committee (G. A. Committee) and then to full court of the High Court Division and upon receiving the report from the Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court, rejected the writ petition summarily on the ground that the recommendations sent from the Ministry of Law were submitted before the full court. Later the petitioner upon finding that the proposal of the initial suspension order was neither placed before the General Administration Committee nor to the full court as mandated under Rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules, preferred the instant writ petition challenging the entire proceeding against him along with the second show cause notice and obtained the instant rule nisi. 

 7. The petitioner is a judicial officer recruited in BCS (judicial) Cadre as government servant serving in the subordinate judiciary as Senior Assistant Judge and posted at Chuadanga at the relevant time and as such he is amenable to the provision of Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 1985. The controlling authority of the petitioner. the Ministry of Law when suspected that the petitioner acted in contravention of the provision of Section 3(d) of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rule 1985. decided to proceed in disciplinary action against the petitioner and accordingly upon observing all preliminary formalities sent correspondence for obtaining approval from the Supreme Court as Article 116 of the Constitution requires such approval. Annexure N(1) manifest that the Ministry of Law through the Senior Assistant Secretary sent a letter on 10.8.2000 to the Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court Respondent No.2 praying for Approval for placing the petitioner on suspension prior to initiation of the departmental proceedings against him. This court, in order to satisfy itself about the actual step taken in the Supreme Court concerning the petitioner, called for and brought the record from the office of Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court, Respondent No.2 and examined the same. It appears from the said record that the Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court, Respondent No.2 upon receiving the said letter dated 10.08.2000, initiated office note for the purpose of approval of the said proposal enunciated in Annexure-N(1) and obtained the approval of the Hon'ble Chief Justice on 27.8.2000. Annexure-D manifest that the Ministry of Law upon receiving such approval of the Hon'ble Chief Justice, issued the order of suspension of the petitioner under the signature of Senior Assistant Secretary to be effective during the pendency of the departmental proceedings. 

 8. The learned Senior Counsel Barrister Moinul Hosein appearing on behalf of the writ petitioner while taken this court through the Annexure-N(2) develops his argument that the Respondent No.2 upon receiving Annexure-N ( 1) although initiated the office note and placed the same before the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh, with a proposal whether the suspension of the writ petitioner should be recommended or not, the Hon'ble Chief Justice accorded his approval by endorsing 'হ্যাঁ' at the bottom of the note sheet which cannot be treated as compliance of rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules, The learned Smear Counsel Barrister Hosein argues that provision of Article 116 of the Constitution requires that the approval must be obtained from the Supreme Court prior to suspension of any subordinate judicial officer and the procedure for obtaining such approval is embodied in Rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules Part-I Chapter-I which mandates that any such proposal for suspension or dismissal of the subordinate judicial officer shall he placed before the full court of the High Court, Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court through the General Administration Committee known as G. A. Committee which having not been complied with in the instant case, the suspension of the writ petitioner from the service and the initiation of departmental proceeding being No.3 of 2000 and 4 of 2000 cannot be sustained under the Constitutional guarantee as embodied under Article 27 of the Bangladesh Constitution. 

 9. On the other hand the learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Md. lqbal Hossain upon referring the endorsement of the honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh at the bottom of the note sheet dated 27.08.2000 strenuously argues that through such endorsement the highest authority of the Bangladesh Supreme Court has accorded its permission and as such the same is the approval of the Bangladesh Supreme Court which must be treated as an approval accorded pursuant to the provision Article 116 of the Constitution and as such no violation of constitutional guarantee has occurred in placing the petitioner under suspension. 

 10. Annexure N(1) is a letter dated 10.08.2000 sent by the Ministry of Law, under the signature of Senior Assistant Secretary praying for approval of the proposal to place the petitioner under suspension. The content of Annexure-N(2) is reproduced below: 

 Upon receiving Annexure N(1)  it appears that the Respondent No.2 initiated in sheets regarding the approval of the proposed suspension and initiation of departmental proceeding against the writ petitioner and the said file was placed before the honorable Chief Justice who accorded his approval by endorsing his opinion 'হ্যাঁ' at the bottom of the note sheet dated 27.8.2000. 

 11. Now the question arose whether the aforesaid approval of the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh by endorsing 'হ্যাঁ' can be treated as approval accorded by the Supreme Court within the meaning of Article 116 of the Constitution read with the provision of Rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules. 

 Article 116 of the Constitution mandated the government in the Ministry of Law to submit such proposal for suspension and initiation of departmental proceeding against any subordinate judicial officer before the Supreme Court of Bangladesh for its approval. Rule 3(d) of the High Court Rules conferred power upon the General Administration Committee of the High Court Division to deal with such proposal and to arrange for according the recommendation of the Supreme Court upon such proposal. Rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules provides as follows; 

 (d) to make recommendations for the appointment of Subordinate Judges and for the promotion, degradation, or suspension of Subordinate Judges and Munsifs; . but all such recommendations of the Administration committee shall be placed before the Full Court for approval." 

 The simple and operational meaning of rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules is that if any proposal for promotion, degradation and suspension of any subordinate judicial officer is sent from the Ministry of lava for approval by the Supreme Court the General Administration Committee of the High Court Division upon receiving it, shall make its recommendation upon it and then place the same before the full court of the High Court Division for approval. The entire power and function of general Administration committee of the High Court Division has been detailed in Chapter 1, Part 1 of the General rules of the High Court Division Rules wherefrom this court finds no deviated provision upon which, by any chance, it could be presumed that such proposal for 'Suspension of the petitioner may not he submitted to the full court. 

 13. From the record of the writ petitioner, kept in the office of respondent No.2, this court finds that his Lordships the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh upon considering the note sheet, submitted by the Additional Registrar on 27.8.2000 Annexure7N(2) only accorded his permission by endorsing ‘হ্যাঁ’ at the bottom of the note sheet and from no where of the said record this court finds any attempt to place the said proposal either to the General Administration Committee or through them to the full court of the High Court Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court. This endorsement of ‘হ্যাঁ’ is directed to the operative portion of the note sheet. Annexure-N(2), wherein the initiator of the note sheet instead of proposing whether the letter sent by the Ministry of Law. Annexure-N(1), should be placed before the G.A. Committee wrote the following proposal most erroneously; 

 From the said record at page 23 this court finds another note sheet initiated by the Additional Registrar of the High Court Division on 06.01.2000 on the proposal sent by the Ministry of Law regarding initiation of departmental proceeding in Case No.3 of 2000 against the petitioner. Wherefrom it appears that his Lordships the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh accorded his permission by endorsing at the bottom of the note sheet in ‘হ্যাঁ দুই মাসের মধ্যে বিভাগীয় মোকদ্দমা শেষ করিতে হইবে। In this note sheet the same Additional Registrar of the Supreme Court again committed the same error in the operative portion of the note sheet and as such the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh although passed the said order per incurious but as the provision of Rule-3(d) of the High Court Division mandates that such proposal must be placed before the G. A. Committee, the approval of the Hon'ble Chief Justice through endorsing tantamount to as an approval to place the said proposal for suspension of the petitioner to the G. A. committee. 

 15. It appears that upon approval through the endorsement  হ্যাঁ ' by the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh, two charge sheets under departmental proceeding No.4 of 2000, and departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000 Annexure-E and E(1), have been served upon the petitioner and upon receiving the reply from the writ petitioner on the said charge sheet, one learned District Judge Mr. Azizul Hoque was appointed as Inquiry Officer to hold enquiry into the allegations, as brought through the said charge sheet. The Inquiry Officer upon holding enquiry submitted his report before the Ministry of Law, Annexure-H, stating that the allegations as brought against the petitioner were not proved. Upon receiving the said enquiry report, the government in the Ministry of Law, examined the entire aspect of the case against the writ petitioner and came to the finding that the allegations as brought against the writ petitioner have not been proved beyond reasonable doubt and accordingly the Ministry of Law decided to exonerate the petitioner from the charge leveled against him by dropping the departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000 and 4 of 2000 and also to withdraw the suspension order against the writ petitioner as appears from Annexure-I, the note sheet of the Ministry of Law. 

 16. The learned Senior Advocate Barrister Moinul Hossain in his further ground strenuously argues that the Ministry of Law upon the report of the departmental proceedings against the petitioner since satisfied about the innocence of the petitioner rightly proposed for exoneration of the petitioner and sent the proposal to the Supreme Court for its approval and this time the respondent No.2 although placed the same before the G. A. Committee but the same was that placed before the full court of the High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court despite the refusal of the G. A. Committee to approved the proposal of the Ministry of Law. The learned Senior Advocate Barrister Moinul Hossain vehemently argues that such refusal to exonerate the petitioner from the allegation and to drop the proceeding has the same implication of law and as such the same must also be placed before the full court and therefore the refusal of the G. A. Committee has the effect of legality. 

 18. The proposal to exonerate the petitioner from the allegation brought in the departmental proceedings and for withdrawal of suspension since requires the approval of the Supreme Court the Ministry of Law upon finding such requirement issued and sent two letters, Annexure-H(2) and Annexure-I(2) to the respondent No.2, the Registrar of Bangladesh Supreme Court praying for approval of such proposal from the Supreme Court, Annexure-N(4) manifest that the said two letters as aforesaid, were considered by the General Administration committee, in its meeting on 23.5.2002, where the members of the General Administration Committee refused to recommend such proposal and adopt the following resolution: 

 The aforesaid resolution regarding non-approval of the proposal for exoneration of the petitioner from the charge as levelled against him in departmental proceeding No.4 of 2000 and for dropping the other departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000 since has the effective implication upon the question of suspension and dismissal from service of the member of the subordinate judiciary, the same is also liable to be placed before the full court of Bangladesh Supreme Court under the mandatory provision of  Rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules. But this time also the said resolution of the General Administration Committee was not placed before the Full Court. 

 This supervisory authority of the High Court Division over the subordinate courts and tribunals is exercised by the General Administration Committee, formed under the provision of Rule-I under Part-1, Chapter-1 of the High Court Division rules. Under this Chapter-1 the General Administration Committee of the High Court Division has been entrusted with various functions to be discharged on their own accord and wisdom excepting the function of recommending for appointment of the judicial officers, and for promotion, degradation or suspension of subordinate judges and munsifs (Now Joint District Judges and Assistant Judges) which recommendations must be placed before the full court for approval. Apart from such restriction upon the authority of the (G. A. Committee, rule 16(e) of the High Court Division Rules Part-1, Chapter-1 mandate that before making any recommendation by G. A. committee for the dismissal of the judicial officers, all the judges of the High Court Division must be consulted. The provision of rule 16(e) as aforesaid reads as follows: High Court Division Rules: "Rule-16: On the following matters all the Judges shall be consulted : (e) All recommendations for the dismissal from office of Judicial Officers and all proposals to suspend or dismiss from service any Gazetted Officer." 

 (2) The Supreme Court shall consist of the Chief Justice, to be known as the Chief Justice of Bangladesh, and such number of other Judges as the President may deem it necessary to appoint to each division. 

 (3) The Chief Justice, and the Judges appointed to the Appellate Division, shall sit only in that division and the other Judges shall sit only in the High Court Division. 

 (4) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution the Chief Justice and the other Judges shall be independent in the exercise of their judicial functions." 

 22. Mr. Hasan M. S. Azim appearing on behalf of the writ petitioner along with the Senior Advocate Barrister Moinul Hosein, upon taking permission from this court to add some points, relied upon the decision of the case namely The State -Vs- Chief Editor of Manab Zamin and others reported in 2 LG-1 and argues that their Lordship in the said case has decided the point what is meant by the expression "Full Court" which is relevant for the purpose of deciding the instant point that whether the endorsement by the Hon'ble Chief Justice 'হ্যাঁ' is sufficient as against the decision of the full court. 

 23. In the referred case of the State -Vs-Chief Editor of Manab Zamin and others reported in 2 LG-1 his Lordship Mr. Justice Syed Amirul Islam in a Division Bench of this court while considering the meaning of "Full Court" held as under: "Since we are of the opinion that the opinion of the judiciary in the matter of appointment of judges of this Court should have primacy ire would like to enlighten this feature. To appoint the most appropriate person, as judge of the Court there is no other way without concurrence with the opinion of the Chief Justice. Naturally, a question may arise as to whether the "Chief Justice" denotes a person designata: or the Judiciary. Without hesitation we would like to say that here the connotation of the Chief Justice is the superior judiciary". 

 24. We are in humble agreement with his Lordships in respect of the definition of "Full Court" as his Lordships arrived at since the Supreme Court of Bangladesh means the combination of the judges of the institution with the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh as enunciated in Article 94(2) of the Constitution and therefore the exercise of power under Article 116 of the Constitution requires the approval by all the judges of the Supreme Court in its meeting, known as "Full Court Meeting". But as the supervisory authority upon the Subordinate judiciary is only rendered upon the High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court under the provision of Article 109 of the Constitution, the term "Full Court" so far it relates to rule 3(d) of the High Court Division Rules, Part-1, Chapter-1, shall mean all the judges of the High Court Division including the Hon'ble Chief Justice comprising the Full Court. The honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh is a person designata and the term Supreme Court of Bangladesh shall always include the honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh and all other Judges of the Supreme Court within the meaning Article 94(2) of the Constitution to constitute the Full Court. 

 This Rule has been further assailed on behalf of the Respondent No.2, Registrar of Supreme Court of Bangladesh on the ground that the petitioner earlier preferred Writ Petition No.7316 of 2003 on the self same cause for a direction and withdrawal of his suspension order and a Division Bench of this court heard the motion on 22.3.2004, asked for a report from the Registrar of Supreme Court of Bangladesh as to whether Annexure-J to the said writ petition dated 26.4.2003 addressed to the Registrar, Bangladesh Supreme Court by the Ministry of Law and Parliamentary Affairs, was received by the Registrar of the Supreme Court and whether it was placed before the General Administration Committee (G. A. Committee) as per High Court Rules 3(d) and 16(e) and then to full court and whether any order for or against the petitioner was passed by the full court and upon getting the said report from the Registrar of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, the said Division Bench comprised with his Lordships Mr. Justice Md. Abdul Matin and Mr. Justice Syed Refat Ahmed found from the said report that the decision of withdrawal of the suspension order was referred to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh and the Hon'ble Chief Justice placed it before the General Administration Committee and the General Administration Committee also placed it before the full court and the full court by decision taken on 14.8.2003 refused to review the matter of suspension and the decision of the full court can not be interfered with by that bench. Therefore their lordships also found that the show cause notice as has been issued upon the petitioner was issued as per the direction of the Supreme Court and at that moment no action was taken against the petitioner and since the suspension is not punishment the petitioner being a public servant in the republic is not entitled to file that writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution and his remedy, if any, lies in the administrative tribunal as per the decision made in the case of Secretary, Ministry of Finance Vs Md. Masdar Hossain and others reported in 52 DLR(AD)-82 and as the self same cause has been adjudicated by a Division Bench of this Court the principle of res-judicata is applicable against the instant case and as such the instant rule is liable to be discharged. 

 From the aforesaid underlined portion of the report it appears that the matters which has been mentioned to have been considered by the General Administration Committee is not regarding the proposal for placing the petitioner on suspension and the initiation of the departmental proceedings, rather the report dated 04.04.2004 has mentioned that the proposal for withdrawal of suspension and the exoneration of the petitioner from the departmental proceeding No.3 of 2000 and 4 of 2000 were placed before the General Administration Committee, pursuant to the order passed by the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh. But it appears that the report in its ultimate line categorically said that, as the General Administration Committee did not pass any order for placement of those matter before the full court, the same has not been placed before the full court. 

 Heard the learned advocates of both sides and perused the application and also perused the report submitted by the Registrar of this Court called for by this Bench on 22.03.2004. It appears that the decision of withdrawal of the suspension order was referred to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh and the Hon'ble Chief Justice placed it before the G. A. Committee and G. A. Committee also placed it before the full court and the full court by decision taken on 14.08.2003 refused to review the matter of suspension and the decision of the full court cannot be interfered with by this Bench. Moreover, the show cause notice as has been issued upon the petitioner is as per direction of the Supreme Court. At the moment no action has been taken and suspension is not punishment and petitioner being a public servant in the Republic is not entitled to file this writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution. His remedy if any lies in the Administrative Tribunal Reference may be made to the case of Secretary, Ministry of Finance -Vs- Md. Masdar Hossain and other reported in 52 DLR (AD) 82 wherein it was held :- 

 42. Upon careful examination of the provision of Article -116 read with rule 3(d) of the High Court Rules this court is in firm view that the initiation of any disciplinary action against the person employed in the judicial service of Bangladesh shall be made by the President, through the prescribed authority as authorized under the rules of business, the Ministry of law, but prior to materializing any such decision against such incumbent, consultation with the Supreme Court is a Mandatory provision of the Constitution. Further the provision of Rule 3(d) of the High Court Rules mandates that pursuant to such constitutional provision, the General Administration Committee of the High Court Division will make the recommendation either allowing or refusing the proposal sent by the Ministry of Law and all such proposal shall be placed before the full court of the High Court Division of the Supreme Court for its approval. Moreover, when any proposal for dismissal of the judicial officer is recommended by the General Administration Committee, all the judges of the High Court Division must be consulted on such recommendation. Further when the G. A. Committee has acted under rule 3 of Chapter-1 of the High Court Division Rules and the recommendation made by it was not placed before the full court then the said decision, must be circulated amongst the judges of the High Court Division. 

 43. From the materials on record it appears that the prior to placing the petitioner under suspension, no approval from the full court of the High Court Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court was taken and as such order of suspension, initiation of departmental proceeding and issuance of the 2nd show cause notice is violative of the constitutional provision which being passed by the President of the country is challengeable under the jurisdiction of judicial review. 

 (1) Any proposal for the degradation or suspension of Assistant Judge, Senior Assistant Judges as and any proposal for dismissal from service of the judicial officers must be placed before General Administration Committee (G. A. Committee) of the High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court for recommendation and all such recommendations made by the G. A. Committee must be placed before the Full Court of the High Court Division for finality. 2) The honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh is a person designate and the term Supreme Court of Bangladesh shall always include the honorable Chief Justice of Bangladesh and all other Judges of the Supreme Court within the meaning of Article 94 

 (5) The refusal to reconsider the 3rd proposal of the Ministry of Law by the General Administration Committee of the High Court Division in respect of according approval to exonerate the petitioner from the charge levelled against him and to drop the disciplinary proceeding has been made upon relying on extraneous and irrelevant materials which tentamounts to malice in law.
